Introduction Background EVs are essential in transportation since they offer a twofold benefit because of reduced carbon emissions and enhanced environmental sustainability 1 , 2 . The increasing demand for EVs requires a corresponding increase in an effective charging system. The management systems are designed to maximize the distribution of electrical power in such a way that the users can have an uninterrupted power supply as the demand varies 3 , 4 . Solar PV and wind generation facilities are some of the RESs that will provide sufficient electricity to add to the EV charging stations when demand is on the increase. Green solar panels produce power using sunlight in the day, which enables the generation of clean power, but fluctuating wind energy generates helpful power generation in regions that have a constant wind flow 5 , 6 . One of the most common systems of winding power of the wind energy resources is the Doubly Fed Induction Generator (DFIG) 7 . Renewable-generated power will help the grid to produce sufficient power to support the growing EV demand, besides lessening reliance on traditional power sources 8 . A grid-synchronous EV charging system would be needed to make the grid stable, and this system would synchronize EV charging with the availability of renewable power. Demand response applications will allow vehicle owners to adjust their charging schedule to match times of renewable energy excess to the power grid to achieve stability 9 , 10 . Vehicles-to-Grid (V2G) technologies provide EVs with the capability of providing stored electricity to the grid during the time of increased power demand, which contributes to the strength of power grids 11 . Wind energy that flows through the power grid stabilizes the electricity systems as it encourages the need to reduce the use of fossil fuels. Prediction analysis of both the energy need and renewable power production patterns is more effective in grid power management 12 , 13 . When grid operators coordinate the charging activity with the availability of renewable energy, maximum use of clean energy will be achieved, and the environmental impact of electric vehicle charging will be reduced 14 . The combination of EVs, PV, wind, and V2G systems forms a transportation network, as a result of which sustainability and resilience of the power system will be achieved. The integration will be essential towards developing a clean, dependable energy future due to the increased use of renewable energy 15 . Literature survey Various research investigations on EV charging systems with SG stability have been conducted through diverse techniques and methodologies. The following section includes summaries of selected works. A P Singh et al. 16 proposed a DC Microgrid (MG)-based Electric Vehicle Charging Station (EVCS) that integrates a grid system with an EV and batteries along with solar PV devices and an AI-ANN -powered V2G and Grid-to-Vehicle (G2V) Power Management Controller (PMC). The EVCS facilitates effective power distribution in residential or commercial buildings by supporting two operating modes: The EV works as a power consumer under G2V and as an energy supplier during V2G functions. The AI-ANN-based PMC uses peaceful mode shifts to control energy exchange between the PV system and battery storage, and electric vehicle and grid connection for a sustained DC bus voltage and stronger operations performance. Nouri et al. 17 integrated ANN and PSO in an intelligent fuzzy logic-based charge and discharge management system for EV batteries in V2G systems, which improves energy extraction from solar systems under various irradiation conditions. Aljafari et al. 18 have presented a new MADNN that constrains a Markov decision process in a dynamic pricing and scheduling framework for EV charging station management. By taking into account dynamic pricing and other EV characteristics, the MADNN incorporates a queuing model to effectively plan EV charging, allowing for efficient coordination between energy supply networks and EVs as variable loads. Kalaiselvan et al. 19 have developed the combination of GOA with THDCNN, forming the GOA-THDCNN hybrid approach, which delivered effective management solutions for integrated PV-solar and small hydro power and EV charging systems. The approach aimed to reach its objectives through plug-in electric device grid connection, bidirectional grid isolation, and hybrid PV network injection-based grid-tied load management and decentralized technology-enabled smart distribution. Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) operation with control features enables this method to achieve effective performance. Maguluri et al. 20 have introduced that a MADQN algorithm serves as a management approach that optimizes the electrical system by distributing EV loads for balance. Deep reinforcement learning and cooperative decision-making mechanisms within MADQN allow the system to enhance the performance of EV battery charge plans. The system uses dynamic response mechanisms to follow power requirements, renewable energy availability, and system constraints, which enable optimized load management with minimal environmental consequences. Pratap et al. 21 have presented that the HAVOGO served as a hybrid optimization method to achieve optimal designs of extensive distribution systems. HAVOGO optimizes the power distribution network integration of EVCSs through a smart fusion of AVO’s structural strength with GO’s flexible design capabilities.
